profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Chicago CH2, is located at 275 Pierce Rd, Itasca, IL 60143, directly adjacent to NTT's original CH1 building on the same Itasca, DuPage County campus. The operator publishes 126,000 square feet of data floor space and 36 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building, describing it in its own newsroom materials as a newer addition to the campus; no formal certifications or specific opening year are stated on the page. Together, CH1 and CH2 account for 72 of the roughly 200-plus megawatts NTT describes for its full Chicago-area campus, implying substantial additional capacity in further campus buildings.

Illinois's data center tax incentive program has become a flashpoint for state energy policy. Governor JB Pritzker announced on June 5, 2026 a temporary suspension of new awards under the state's Data Center Investment Program, citing grid strain; ComEd's CEO stated the program had added roughly $12 a month to the average residential bill over the prior four years. ComEd's northern Illinois service territory is separately projected to face capacity shortfalls beginning around 2029 as data center demand grows, a dynamic pushing new development toward Chicago's southern suburbs where power is more readily available, according to legal-industry analysis of ComEd's planning filings.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. The operators own current Chicago area locations overview page, also fetched this session, independently names CH1, CH2, and CH3 as active facilities on a campus with a planned 200 plus MW of IT load once fully built out, corroborating CH2 as a real, current facility.

reading.body:
NTT Chicago CH2 is a 36 MW facility in Itasca, Illinois, confirmed by the operator's published specifications. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, this capacity represents roughly 900 racks of IT equipment across 126,000 square feet of technical space. The facility is part of a multi-building campus on Pierce Road that the operator has announced will reach 200 MW or more of IT load once fully built out, making it one component of a significantly larger infrastructure project underway in the Chicago area.

Illinois has published capacity totaling 236 MW across six facilities with confirmed specifications from operator sources. NTT Chicago CH2 ranks seventh by published megawatts in the state, placing it below the current published leaders but within a small set of quantified capacity at a time when most of the 44 mapped facilities in Illinois publish no figures. The state context does not indicate how Chicago CH2's capacity compares to the full buildout announced for the campus or to typical data center deployments serving AI workloads.

The facility's scale and operator assignment make it relevant to track as AI deployment patterns emerge. NTT is one of the world's largest telecommunications and IT services providers, with a global data center business. No information is published about which tenants occupy NTT Chicago CH2, the power supply route, or whether grid constraints currently affect its operation or expansion plans.
